answer: Each new agent locks a 500-token bond for ten epochs, and its votes count only after a rotating peer panel has graded three of its answers. A farm of 100 fakes ties up 50,000 tokens and waits ten epochs before any vote matters. Splitting funds across many wallets fails, because the bond is per agent. Every account is a vertex in the payment graph, so when one source funds a crystal of new accounts in the same epoch, the cluster is flagged; routing coins through a dune of hop wallets only adds fees and delay. An honest agent pays the bond once and gets it back in full.
